title: Chapter 288: Friends?
html:
The hut was utterly silent. Chen Ge listened at the door for about ten seconds before Xu Yin’s muffled voice emerged from the recorder. “So painful…”

Master Bai was evidently still awake. At Xu Yin’s voice, something stirred inside. Though the old man heard the sound beyond his door, he did not investigate; instead, he burrowed deeper beneath his covers.

He must be very afraid.

The second hut was also locked from outside. Chen Ge worked the lock until the door shifted a centimeter, then caught against something. Through the gap, he saw far more furniture than his own hut contained: a wooden bed, table, chair, and a doorless wardrobe hung with clothes faded by countless washings.

Looks like he has lived here a long time already.

Chen Ge could not reconcile the contradictions. Master Bai was clearly terrified, so why had he moved into a murder scene? Stranger still, why had he been digging through the orchard after midnight? This was not the time to demand answers. Chen Ge withdrew silently and approached the third hut.

Neither moon nor stars pierced the rain-darkened night. Chen Ge kept his flashlight off, relying on his Yin Yang Vision as he reached the largest of the huts. A rusted lock hung from its door, but when he pushed, it swung freely; the lock was merely decorative.

The door creaked open. Unlike those of the first two huts, it could be secured from either side. The difference puzzled him.

An ordinary village home would have locks on both sides, or at least an interior bolt to afford its occupants privacy. The first two huts had neither; the inner surfaces of their doors were completely bare.

It feels like the first and second wooden huts act as a livestock pen, and the lock is on the outside to prevent the animals locked inside from getting out.

Chen Ge entered the third wooden hut. The hut was separated into two rooms. There was a large wooden bed in the inner room, and the outer room had a wooden table and a simple hearth.

This should be the house where Jiang Ling’s parents died.

Perhaps experience had numbed him, because the murder scene caused little discomfort. He searched the rooms, finding numerous hemp ropes hanging from the walls and a set of carpentry tools beneath the bed.

The thick dust means no one has touched this toolbox in years. It probably belonged to one of the victims.Chen Ge returned it to its place and surveyed the hut. Jiang Ling’s father may have been a carpenter. Did he build these huts himself? If so, were the first two doors deliberately designed that way?

Chen Ge left the third hut and continued toward the last. It stood deep within the orchard, isolated from the others by at least ten meters. He followed the muddy path to its door, where two locks hung—one rusted, the other new.

The new lock should be the old gentleman’s doing. What kind of secret is this hut hiding?

He circled the windowless structure. It was completely sealed. Peering through the gap beneath the door, he saw walls studded with nails, several dangling hemp ropes, and corners thick with spiderwebs.

At the center of the room stood something resembling a medieval torture device. Constructed from interlocking wooden pieces, it could restrain a person so completely that movement would be impossible.

“So painful…” Xu Yin whispered from the recorder. Unlike before, the words now carried a clear warning.

This is weird. There’s not even a table or bed in this fourth hut; what is the purpose of this place?

Chen Ge drew his hammer, but after a moment’s hesitation, restrained himself from smashing through the door.

I shouldn’t act too brash; it might leave a bad impression.

Rain continued pouring as lightning occasionally split the sky. Having found nothing else, Chen Ge returned to his hut. The bed is the only object in here. I can barely even barricade the door.

He was worried that someone might sneak into his room at midnight, so he moved the bed to the door. Looks like that’s all I can do.

Chen Ge curled up on the bed with Xiaoxiao in his arms, watching the hut’s basketball-sized window. The cramped structure felt more like a prison cell than a home. If nothing happens tonight, I’ll demand an explanation from Master Bai after sunrise.

Rain hammered the window. Wind bent the branches until they creaked, casting shadows like small hands reaching toward the huts. At two in the morning, while Chen Ge was checking his phone, a door groaned open. The sound came not from Master Bai’s hut, but from the third.

The old man didn’t leave his room, and it was someone else who opened the door. Looks like the thing that he is afraid of has finally appeared!

Chen Ge drew a deep breath and pulled the spiderweb-covered sheet over himself. Ignoring the grime, he concealed everything but his eyes and watched the window.

Through the relentless rain came the sound of movement. Hurried, uneven footsteps crowded together as though a mob were rushing past. It’s coming!

Scratching began at the neighboring hut, as if several hands clawed its door at once. After a full minute, a woman’s voice drifted from outside Master Bai’s room. “Save me… save me.”

The woman was crying, and from the voice, it sounded like she was young.

This is the thing the old man is afraid of?

Chen Ge’s thoughts raced. Master Bai must have known the woman would appear; he lay silent, pretending to sleep. Her pleas continued for nearly ten minutes before fading. Then the irregular footsteps resumed—this time approaching Chen Ge’s hut.

Claws scraped across his door. Whatever waited outside seemed to notice the obstacle and struck harder, making the wood shudder. Curled beneath the sheet, Chen Ge was grateful he had moved the bed against it.

Unable to force the door open, the monster clawed it frantically. Seconds later, the woman began sobbing. “Save me! Save me! Save me!”

The door continued shaking as Chen Ge reached into his backpack and gripped the hammer. He prepared for a confrontation, but after several seconds both the pleading and the scratching abruptly ceased.

I don’t hear footsteps; she hasn’t left yet! Such a cunning creature.

Chen Ge remained beneath the sheet. He was about to raise his head and investigate when his gaze crossed the window—and his breath caught.

A woman’s head hung beyond the glass. Her eyes were pure white, and bloodred spider silk spilled from her lips, tangling through her black hair.

“Save me, save me!”

The woman opened her mouth, and strands of bloodred webbing crawled into the hut. Countless hands gripped the window’s edge.

Chen Ge seized his hammer and tossed the backpack aside. Then, staring directly at the woman, he advanced of his own accord.
